newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks gain, upward trend seen sustained.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks gain, upward trend seen sustained.

text.p: Croatian stocks posted new mild gains in somewhat slower trade on Thursday, and traders foresaw a sustained upward trend over the next week or so.
"We are talking about a short-term climb, with no special favourites," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage told Reuters.
Other traders outlined stronger interest in some seaside hotel stocks which could fuel their growth after positive signals about this year's tourist season.
Eight of 13 active issues rose on Thursday, two fell, two ended flat and one made a bourse debut.
Volume shrank slightly to 17,146 units and turnover was halved at 6.7 million kuna as the most expensive Zagrebacka Banka ordinary stock did not trade at all.
Its 1/10 global depository receipts (GDRs) traded at $33.45-$33.5 on London's Seaq International.
Most shares seemed to take heart from Franjo Tudjman's clear, albeit expected, victory at the presidential polls which spurred more buying, particularly from foreign investors.

"The market is now recovering from recent losses, caused by the political problems preceding the (presidential) election," Kos added. He referred to international pressure on the government to guarantee the safety of Serb refugees returning to their pre-war homes after violent incidents.
Food processor Podravka, selling 4,462 shares, was the most active stock. It closed at 283 kuna, two down from Wednesday.
Top gainer textile firm Varteks added 10.5 kuna to 73, but it sold only six shares.
Blue chip drugs firm Pliva added six kuna to 501 with 3,832 units sold. Its GDRs fetched $16.75 in London earlier today, but later receded to $16.55.
Other gainers included brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, a subsidiary of Chile's Cervecerias Unidas, up 45 kuna to a record 405 on volume of 659 units.
Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka's ordinaries firmed three kuna to 210 on volume of 681 and confectioner Kras added five kuna to end at 445 with 1,937 shares sold.
The bigger of two decliners, hotelier Suncani Hvar, edged down two kuna to close at 55 on volume of 1,500 shares.
Trading for the first time ever was cutlery-maker Kordun from Karlovac with 2,418 shares at 145 kuna each in what appeared to be a pre-arranged deal.
